_meta.title: Input Document Rules — reading the writer-provided .docx files
_meta.purpose: Machine-readable form of 00_Input_WordDoc_Interpretation_Rules.md: which parts of the Writers Template + Media List are real content, which are boilerplate to discard, how the docx is turned into the marker-text intermediate form, and how the media table's columns are recognised. DocxExtractor.js and MediaListParser.js read this file; nothing about input shapes is hard-coded.
_meta.extension_rule: New boilerplate block, new media-table column heading, new red shade, new template signature = a data edit HERE, never a code change.
_meta.precedence: Where 00-PageForge v1 docs disagree with this file or 00_Input_WordDoc_Interpretation_Rules.md, this file wins.

content_start.rule: Real module content starts at the first RED span that opens the document. Detection chain, first hit wins: (1) LITERAL — a bracket fragment whose folded text is exactly one of content_start_fragments; (2) CANONICAL — the first red span whose primary tag resolves to one of content_start_canonicals (Fundamentals templates open with [Fundamental content] / [Fundamental 1 code] / a bare [Title] instead of [TITLE BAR] — verified on ARFUN01, MXFUN03, EXPFUN04); (3) NONE — convert ALL blocks and surface a loud summary warning (PageForge's own fallback). Everything before the start is template front-matter: not interpreted, not converted, not flagged.
content_start.fallback_note: Last chance before the convert-everything fallback: the first RED span whose primary resolves to one of these directive classes opens the document (EXPFUN06 opens at a bare [H1]; ART1005 similar — verified 12/06/26). Front-matter red spans ([tags] rows, damaged brackets) resolve to nothing, so they can never trigger this.
content_start.note: Mid-document, the looser aliases (title/overview/introduction) are headings, never document starts (Tag_Normalisation_Spec.md page-boundary rule 4) — only the FIRST resolving span opens the document.
content_start._fragments_dropdown_note: (The PNR101 family.) The MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' bilingual template opens at [Content for DROP DOWN MENU] — recognised as a content start so the menu/overview is not trimmed as front matter. Kept in its OWN list (not content_start_fragments) so env REODROPMENU_OFF can switch the whole drop-down-menu template off cleanly. The exact bracketed marker occurs only in PNR101/102/104.

table_row_boundary_markers._note: (As in PMT101, the MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' template written as ONE table.) PNR107 and the other MTK modules carry the page / lesson boundary markers ([MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1], [END OF PAGE], [LESSON N CONTENT], [END OF DROP DOWN MENU]) as PARAGRAPHS between one bilingual table per page; PMT101's writer kept the whole module in one English ║ Māori table and typed those markers as ROWS (the left cell holds the red span, the right cell is empty). IsContentStart reads paragraphs only, so without this no content start would be seen and the module would be refused as 'no Writers Template'. DocxExtractor.PromoteTableRowMarkers runs first in ModuleResolver.PrepareRun's classify loop (the ONE shared prep choke point) and splits a table at every row whose non-empty cells are each exactly ONE red span resolving to a promote_tags canonical and nothing else, emitting the marker as a paraBlock between the two table halves — which turns PMT101's block stream into exactly PNR107's shape; recognition, TrimFrontMatter, the drop-down rescue, the page splitter and the bilingual handlers are all unchanged. Marker-only rows of this kind occur only in PMT101; for every other document the block list is returned as the SAME array, a no-op by construction. NOT promoted, deliberately: the [TITLE BAR] ║ [TITLE BAR] rows of the MTK modules (a content row the bilingual path already reads; 'title bar' is absent from promote_tags), and any row carrying a marker beside other text (ENGS202's page-opener table, the layout-table fence). Env ROWMARKER_OFF turns this off.

module_intro_rescue._doc: THE MODULE INTRODUCTION IS NEVER FRONT MATTER. A template with no literal [TITLE BAR] opens at chain step 2's first red span resolving to the 'lesson content' canonical — the Fundamentals [Fundamental 1 code] opener. On a few templates (ART1004, TWHK902, SSFUN02) that span is a LESSON's [Lesson content] lying AFTER the template's own [MODULE INTRODUCTION] — each opening [H1] Tirohanga Whānui | Overview → the overview → [MODULE INTRODUCTION] → the lessons — so the whole overview and introduction would be trimmed as template front matter and appear on no page. Constraint 1 + KB 01B (the [MODULE INTRODUCTION] is the overview page's body): after the drop-down and title-bar-table rescues, when the start is not a title-bar start and a [MODULE INTRODUCTION] paragraph lies before it, the document opens at the first structural red span (content_start_fallback_directives) when that span precedes the [MODULE INTRODUCTION], else at the [MODULE INTRODUCTION]. Env MIRESCUE_OFF.

recognise_wt._doc: LooksLikeWritersTemplate reads PARAGRAPH-level red tags, so a Writers Template that types EVERY tag — its [TITLE BAR] included — inside bilingual table cells (TRR115) would be refused as 'no Writers Template' before this opener could run. A table cell whose red span resolves to 'title bar' identifies the Writers Template too (the same predicate as the opener).

table_title_bar_opener._doc: The MTK bilingual Writers Template (the TRR family) types its [TITLE BAR] inside a bilingual TABLE cell (English ║ Māori, the row right after the Subject / Course / Module Code table). IsContentStart reads paragraphs only, so the chain would find a LATER start — [LESSON 1 CONTENT] (TRR102 / 103 / 109 / 111), [LESSON 2 CONTENT] (TRR106 / 304), a later paragraph [TITLE BAR] (TRR110) or, with no standard start, the fallback's first paragraph tag (TRR107 an [Image] in lesson 2, TRR108 [H3] Karakia, TRR112 / 113 the [H1] after [Lesson 1], TRR114 [Alert Solid], TRR116 a [Side Alert] in LESSON 5) — and every block between would be trimmed as front matter: the whole overview (Strand / Dispositions / Key objectives / Critical point / Learning intentions / Introduction tables) and, in TRR116 / TRR107 / TRR304, whole lessons. So when a TABLE block holds a cell whose red span resolves to the 'title bar' canonical and it sits BEFORE the start the chain (and the drop-down rescue) found — or no start was found — the document opens at that table. The shape exists only in TRR / PNR; PNR101–107 and TRR203 / 301 open at [Content for DROP DOWN MENU] BEFORE their title-bar table, so they are unaffected by construction. Env TABLETB_OFF turns this off.

front_matter_blocks_documentation: MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE / WRITERS TEMPLATE title block
Section B — New Content Development header + writer-guidance box
'Adjust the italicised text below' instruction lines
NOTE: this list is documentation only — the [TITLE BAR] boundary above is the actual discard mechanism (the list is never exhaustive).

red_runs.rule: A docx run is RED when its w:color val (lowercased) is in red_hex_values. Consecutive red runs in a paragraph merge into ONE red span, wrapped in the markers below — reproducing the exact intermediate form the validated corpus pipeline was built on.

bridge._doc: THE BRACKET BRIDGE: a tag the writer opened in BLACK whose red word carries no bracket and whose ']' lies LATER in the paragraph — 'Te Whatu Ora [' + red 'Hover' + ' – Health New Zealand.]' (HPFUN301), 'features [' + red 'hovertrigger:' + definition + red ']' (ENFUN02). The '[' goes to the red word and a BLACK closing ']' (the first bracket found walking forward, at most max_chars, no line break, no second '[') becomes its own red piece — the scanner's split-bracket form red '[word' + black DEFINITION + red ']' that already renders XDLS502's '[hover' hapori ']' as an infoTrigger. No close found → nothing moves. Merging the whole span into one red run instead would break that working form. Env BRACKETBRIDGE_OFF.

bracket_donation._doc: THE BRACKET SPLIT ACROSS COLOURS: a black run ENDING in a lone '[' hands it to the red run that follows when that red text holds more ']' than '[' (ARFUN04 3L 'Give it a try! Balance exploration [' + red 'insert item#80: images]'); a black run STARTING with a lone ']' hands it to the red run before it when that red text holds more '[' than ']' (TRR114 '] Waiata - You tube'). The tag is whole again and parses as the writer's tag instead of leaving the bracket in learner text (the human-built pages almost never carry an unbalanced bracket). Env BRACKETDONATE_OFF turns this off.

hyperlinked_tag_runs._link_target_note: THE THIRD FENCE: a hyperlinked media tag counts only when its link TARGET is a media-file carrier — the hosts that carry almost all hyperlinked bracket runs (drive / sharepoint / istock / youtube / docs) or a URL with a media file extension. BLL262's `[Audio]` links a tahurangi.education.govt.nz School-Journal resource PAGE (the reading-book family): read as an audio element it would let the carousel composer half-build three identical page placeholders where the honest hand-off box stands; it stays the black link line.
hyperlinked_tag_runs._head_words_note: `embed` is deliberately NOT listed: the only hyperlinked `[embed …]` runs in the corpus are BLL262/BLL263's `[Embed audio book]` — a SharePoint Word-doc link inside a `[Carousel]`, the reading-book family whose honest form is the hand-off box; as a recognised embed element the carousel composer would half-build it (the Word doc as an iframe slide + a web page as an image slide). They stay black link lines, the box stays.
hyperlinked_tag_runs._note: The BLL phonics writers type a media tag AS A HYPERLINK — `[audio 1]` in the hyperlink blue (1155cc / 3494ba / 0563c1) or black, linked to the sound file on Drive / SharePoint — so it is invisible to the tag detector (only red runs are scanned, plus the near-red band) and would render as literal text. A run INSIDE a w:hyperlink whose text carries a bracket whose FIRST WORD is in head_words counts as red. THE FENCE (head_words): those same writers hyperlink EVERY WORD of a phonics word list — [scissors], [wrist], [hedgehog] … content the gold renders as click-to-hear audioTrigger words — and MXDI201 links [Number and Operations] to a curriculum page; a blanket rule would turn them into red instruction spans. Most hyperlinked bracket runs are audio, then audiovisual / av, with a few image, video and embed. THE SECOND FENCE (exclude_words): a bracket whose words after the head include one of these is NOT a media tag — the XDLS903/904/905 `[Audio Animation N: <sharepoint script> Note this will be repeated across five units]` lines are a CS-produced animation brief (the CL-0037 class), and routing them to the audio element would render a bare .mp3 player and LOSE the writer's link + note; they stay the literal link line + Writers Note. The block a hyperlinked tag run fires on is marked block.hyperTag (a side-channel, never in the text) so MediaBuilder.media can render the words the writer typed inside the same hyperlink (Emit_Templates elements.media_hyperlinked_lead). Strictly additive; the hyperlink target still rides block.links. Env HYPERTAG_OFF turns this off.

near_red_tag_runs._note: A writer's structural [tag] typed in a NON-STANDARD RED would render as literal text if only runs whose w:color is in red_hex_values were scanned for tags. Nearly all tag brackets are ff0000/ee0000, but some sit in a NEAR-RED the list does not name — ed0000 (the HIS NCEA1 writer), fa0000 (ENGFUN02), c00000 (Word's standard Dark Red — the OS* / CED / ARFUN / TEFUN writers), ed1c24, f72b2b; the gold renders every one of them as its tag. THE FENCE (require_bracket): a near-red run counts as red ONLY when it carries a [ or ] — because c00000 is also used for CONTENT (MXFU302 '+ 5 = 9', ENGI401 'tone' / 'pace', ENGS301) and a blanket rule would turn that content into stripped red-text instructions. Strictly additive: no run in red_hex_values changes, no bracket-less run changes. Hue band: r >= min_r AND g <= max_g AND b <= max_b (c0504d — Word's Accent-2 — falls outside on g). The exact list above stays the primary rule. Env NEARRED_OFF turns this off.

marker_tail_letters._doc: THE WRITER'S RED FIRST LETTERS AFTER A RED MARKER BELONG TO THE WORD (KB constraint 1: the writer's characters are never deleted). A writer types a red marker and keeps red for the first letter or two of the next word: «[definition: » ‹O›«utside of Aotearoa…», «[button]» ‹S›«ubmit», «[multi choice image activity]» ‹C›«lick the emoji…». The red runs merge into ONE marker span, so the letters become the marker's tail and the word ships cut («ctions to reduce the effects.», «lick the emoji»). When the merged span's LAST red run is 1 to max_chars letters with no space after it, the black text right after it opens with a lowercase letter, and the span before those letters holds a «[» or «(» and ends at a boundary (a space, colon, bracket or parenthesis), the letters go back to the start of the black word — also when the writer typed the marker's closing «]» black after the definition («[insert rollover definition: » ‹F› «riendships between countries or groups.]»): the word is whole either way. Env REDTAILLETTER_OFF.

layout_instruction_line._doc: THE WRITER'S LAYOUT INSTRUCTION TYPED IN BLACK (KB constraint 37: a writer's instruction to the developer is a red Writers Note, never learner text). A writer heads the module menu with «Tab Nav layout with the following layout:» in BLACK and lists the page's tabs in a one-cell table after it («**Introduction** / **Agency** / … [IMAGE: image23.png]»): both shipped in the menu as learner text, although the page's side tabs are built from the content itself. A black paragraph matching line_pattern becomes a red instruction (the Writers Note); when the next block is a table of no more than max_cells cells, its words (image tokens removed) join the note and the table leaves the page. Other writers type the same instruction red — it is already a note.

tagged_learner_line._doc: THE LEARNER LINE TYPED ALL IN RED AFTER ITS OWN TAG (KB constraint 1: the writer's words are never lost). A writer sometimes colours a whole learner paragraph red, its tag included — «[body] Select the best word to end these sentences to fit the rhythm.», «[body] We use words like:» — so the words sit inside the tag's red span and the tag has no black text: the body element rendered nothing (the line was lost) or the line became a developer note. When a paragraph is ONE red span whose bracket is a tag in `bracket_pattern` and whose words after the bracket are a learner sentence — at least min_words words, ending as `end_pattern` says, no instruction cue (Instruction_Cues), nothing `deny_pattern` names (a module code, an address, another bracket) — the words become the tag's text. A developer line of the same shape («[body] CS: scramble the sayings …», «[body] from PHO1031 Lesson 2 & 1») stays a note.
tagged_learner_line._cue_note: The instruction-cue test ignores the two layout words a learner line also uses («… Click below to find out how.»); a line that opens with a build verb («Put the two boxes below in some fancy looking box so it stands out a bit.») is the writer talking to the developer and stays a note.
tagged_learner_line._deny_note: A line opening in a round bracket is the writer's aside to the developer («[body] (not sure if we should put the method here or in the workbook, what will look better?)»), never the learner line; a module code («from PHO1031 Lesson 2 & 1»), an address or another bracket marks a developer reference.

red_runs.bridge_split_tag_note: Word can split a single uniform-RED [tag] into separate runs and DROP the colour on an interior space, fragmenting ONE tag across two [RED TEXT] marker spans (ANZH304 '[Please embed this journal story (as in ANZHFUN01 phase 2]'). DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph's red-merge loop BRIDGES a stray non-red whitespace run that sits MID-TAG between two red runs — fires ONLY when the red text so far has an unbalanced '[' (mid-tag) AND the gap run is whitespace-only AND the next run is red, so it reassembles ONE split tag but NEVER merges across real black content (an intentional '[tag: black label]' form) or between two complete tags. The COMMON same-colour split (Word's usual run fragmentation, e.g. '[Tab 1: I'+'ntroduction'+']' -> [Tab 1: Introduction]) is merged by the consecutive-red loop — this adds only the whitespace-gap variant, which is rare. env REDBRIDGE_OFF turns it off.

red_label_text._doc: Constraint 1; a family dialect keyed to the MX series (with the red-label mechanism). The MX writers type the LEARNER's instruction in red behind an 'Akonga Instructions:' label ('Akonga Instructions: Check your skill of reading data from a table …' — MXDB301, MXDI301 (label red, text black), MXEO102; the label occurs in no other family). Treated as a normal instruction it would become a developer-facing Writers Note (the learner would never see the instruction) or a stray 'Writers Note: Akonga Instructions:'; the gold renders the text as an ordinary learner paragraph and drops the label. For a module matching code_patterns, ContentConverter.#instrNote renders a writer instruction opening with label_pattern as the learner's paragraph(s), the label dropped, where the free §5.16 whole-span instruction's red Writers Note would go. A line a widget capture holds stays the developer's note: in hand-off mode the 'before the box' place is inside the collapsed reference-code box (a learner paragraph there is still developer-only, and would enlarge the capture). Skipped when the text holds a bracketed tag. Env AKONGALABEL_OFF.

red_label_tag._doc: The supervisor-note box + constraint 1 (the same family as the supervisor-note spelling aliases). An UNBRACKETED red supervisor label at a paragraph head — 'Supervisor’s Notes: Support your ākonga …' / 'Supervisor: Guide your ākonga …' typed wholly red (MXEO102: otherwise dev-facing Writers Notes, the supervisor's text off the page), or 'Supervisor note:' / 'Supervisor’s Notes:' red before black text or alone on its line (MXEO202, MXFL104, BLL110, BLL130: otherwise «Writers Note: Supervisor note:» + a plain paragraph) — is the writer's [Supervisor note]: the paragraph's first red run matching label_pattern is rewritten as the red tag (tag) and the paragraph's remaining words, red or black, as black text; skipped when that remainder holds a bracketed tag. Env REDLABEL_OFF.

structural._doc:
THE BLACK-TYPED STRUCTURAL MARKER IS THE WRITER'S TAG. The black-tag rule promotes a black [Hn] at a paragraph head; a STRUCTURAL marker typed black would otherwise stay text: ANZH104's `__**[MODULE INTRODUCTION]**__` (bold-underline — the black-tag pattern takes one wrapper) would render as the literal

[MODULE INTRODUCTION]

with the introduction in the menu and an empty body; HIS1002 / SSCI104 carry a black `[End page]`. [TITLE BAR] is NOT promoted: TEFUN02 / 05's black one is a duplicate inside the front-matter info area (a second title bar would open a sub-document, AR-4). KB constraint 5 (no literal tag) + constraint 1 + the writer's own page / lesson tag: these canonicals are promoted as the black-tag rule does, the head pattern accepting one or two emphasis wrappers; a promoted marker whose remainder is only the closing wrappers drops them. Env BLACKSTRUCT_OFF.
structural._not_lesson: [LESSON N] is deliberately not listed: HIS1002's ten black `[LESSON N] TITLE` lines sit right before a RED [Lesson Overview] that already opens each lesson page, so promoting them would open an extra implicit page after the overview and misalign every lesson; GEO1006's black [LESSON N] lines are mixed. A black [LESSON N] with no red opener after it is a separate page-split question.

media_after_scan._fence_note: A media line inside a callout's reach stays black: walking back over black items, heading tags, the pass tags and instruction-class items, the nearest other tag is a callouts.by_tag key → skip (HIS1005 6.0: [alert box] → a [body]-parsed writer instruction → [H3] → the black [Image Link] line; converting it emptied the alert on the first probe).
media_after_scan._doc: The media half of the black-tag rule, AFTER the widget scan: PageAssembler.#blackLeadMedia turns an UNCONSUMED black item that opens its paragraph with a black `[Image …]` / `[Video …]` bracket the normaliser resolves to one of `tags` into the tag item a red tag builds, so the image / video emitter renders it — and, because the page's widget scan has already run, no open widget can absorb it (as a click-drop would on DTC1005 18.0). Env BLACKLEADMEDIA_OFF turns this off.

black_lead_tag._tags_note: image / video are deliberately not listed here: a promoted black `[Image – URL]` directly after a click-drop widget would become a widget MEMBER and the walk would swallow the next section (DTC1005 18.0). media_after_scan handles them after the widget scan instead, so a promoted media tag stays out of an open widget.
black_lead_tag._doc: THE BLACK-TYPED TAG. Only red text is scanned for [tags]; a structural tag the writer typed in BLACK at the head of a paragraph (`[H3] Knowledge Check` AGH1006, `[H1] Develop a digital technologies outcome…` DTC1005, `[Image or something similar – https://unsplash…]` DTC1005, `[Video 1] … https://youtu.be/…` CEDR203) would render as literal learner text ([Body] is stripped separately by black_leading_tag_strip). DocxExtractor.PromoteBlackLeadTags re-marks a paragraph's leading black bracket (after optional **/__) as the red run the writer meant when the normaliser resolves it to one of `tags`; a paragraph that opens red and every table cell are untouched. Env BLACKLEADTAG_OFF turns this off.

repair_missing_bracket.rule:
A writer occasionally drops a square bracket off a tag (as in ENGC101-00 'H2] Know:'). TagNormaliser.Parse repairs the two EDGE forms for CLASSIFICATION (a dangling '[x' with no ']', and a leading 'x]' with no '['), but ~10 OTHER red-span consumers (RenderText, the overview-menu partition, the black-tag strip, InteractiveScanner, ...) read the raw bracket structure and would LEAK the literal (a lost 'Know' heading and a '
H2]
' in its place). So the repair happens ONCE at the source: when a CONTENT red span opens with a lone 'x]' (missing the '[') AND the token x resolves to a KNOWN tag by a WHOLE-token match (how in clean_hows — exact / denumbered / denumbered_head; NOT a tag-word EMBEDDED inside writer prose), the missing '[' is inserted into block.text so EVERY downstream consumer sees a well-formed '[x]'. Original case is preserved (RenderText needs it). GENERAL across every tag (lexicon-driven), NOT one module. how=embedded rejects prose/instruction false positives ('that when they click/hover on the letter...' -> audio embedded; 'Please create a dropdown menu for each item]' -> dropdown embedded). The MISSING-CLOSE form ('[hover trigger: ') is deliberately NOT touched: Parse's dangling repair + RenderText's optional ']?' already absorb it. env BRACKETFIX_OFF leaves the literal in place.

red_runs.collapse_whitespace_only_note:
(As in OSBY201-03.) A merged red span whose entire content is WHITESPACE (a writer mis-coloured a space/tab red) is NOT wrapped in a [RED TEXT] marker — it is emitted as a single plain space. Without this, PageSplitter treats the empty marker as a standalone item and FRAGMENTS the paragraph (OSBY201-03 '**Banter is** like playful teasing' split into two

at a red space). A red span with any non-whitespace content (a real [tag]/instruction) is untouched — the strip fires ONLY on pure whitespace, so it can never drop a tag. Read by DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph; env REDWS_OFF turns it off.
red_runs.note: Verified against OSAH401 Writers Template.docx: writers use ff0000 (Word default red) and ee0000. Other colours observed (316757 green, 3494ba blue, 00b050 green, bfbfbf grey) are content emphasis, never tags. New red shade seen in the wild = append the hex here.

table_markers.rule: Docx tables are serialised into the corpus text-table form so the same downstream parsing applies to fresh uploads and the historical parsed corpus.

single_cell._note: THE SINGLE-CELL LAYOUT TABLE. The speech-bubble rule dissolves a table only when a SPEECH BUBBLE shares it with the [Activity], because that bubble is a reliable proxy for 'one cell holds the character, the other holds the activity'. A ONE-ROW ONE-CELL table needs no proxy: there is no second cell for data to live in, so it cannot be widget data — it is a box the writer drew round an activity, and every builder that meets it would read the whole activity as its data table and decline. The shape is rare: ENGI103 ([Activity 1B]), ENGI400 ([Activity 2A], [Activity 2C]) and TEDC402 ([Activity] 1D, the slider) dissolve; the reo cells (TRR112, TRR113) are held out by the prefix fence, because reoMode routes tables through the bilingual handlers. The human build confirms the shape: ENGI400's gold renders 2A and 2C as plain blocks inside their activity boxes, ENGI103's gold renders 1B as its own activity box carrying the supervisor note as a 'super-content row' (and no <table> in the whole module), and TEDC402's gold renders 1D as heading + body + quote + slider + journal button with no table anywhere. The speech-bubble fences carry over unchanged (a PAGE_BOUNDARY/SECTION_MARKER span still refuses; the dissolve still runs before the missing-bracket repair, which is what heals TEDC402's 'Activity]' typo). The interactive tag is not the discriminator; the SHAPE is: widening interactive_tags to 'any INTERACTIVE invocation' would dissolve DATA tables that must stay — CEDO501's 1x4 quiz tables, ENGI400's 6x2 flipCard fronts/backs, TEDC402's own 4x4 flipCard and 5x3/3x3 drag-and-drop option grids, HPFUN901's 3x1 click-drop column and the TRR English|Te Reo pair tables. REQUIRE_EXPLICIT_ACTIVITY_OPENER: the bracket must open with the word 'activity'. HPFUN903's one-cell table contains no opener the writer typed as an activity at all; what makes it 'an activity' is the WIDGET REQUEST '[interactive tool] quiz — tick box yes or no DEV: answers will vary', which merely aliases to the activity tag. Dissolving it would drop the writer's 'DEV: answers will vary' instruction from the page (which §6 forbids) and promote the first bullet into the box's <h3>, a shape the gold never uses. Requiring the word 'activity' separates that case from ENGI400's '[Activity 2A]' and TEDC402's 'Activity] 1D' structurally rather than per-module. Env SBSINGLECELL_OFF turns this arm off alone; SBLAYOUT_OFF turns off the whole rule.

bubble_layout_dissolve._note: Free the speech bubble from the page-layout table. A table whose red spans resolve to BOTH an ACTIVITY-family CONTAINER_OPEN marker AND a speech-bubble INTERACTIVE invocation is a PAGE-LAYOUT table, not widget data: the writer laid the activity out in one cell and the character+balloon in the other, and the HUMAN'S OWN ANSWER is to dissolve the table — the finished page renders the two cells as ordinary stacked blocks in reading order (TEDC402-1.0). DocxExtractor.DissolveBubbleLayoutTables turns each cell into one paragraph block (in-cell ' / ' line breaks restored to plain newlines — the soft-break form), BEFORE the missing-bracket repair so a cell's 'Activity]' typo heals too; the [Activity] opener then opens its box and the [Image]+[speech bubble] cell rides the no-table avatar dialect this module's free-body bubbles already build through. THE FENCE: an activity marker alone is not enough — many tables with one must STAY tables (bilingual TRR embedded-activity tables, fundamentals accordion/slide tables, CEDO501's quiz tables); only tables with BOTH markers dissolve. A table carrying any PAGE_BOUNDARY/SECTION_MARKER span never dissolves (an in-cell [End page] reaching the page splitter would churn pagination — ENGS202's page-opener table stays exactly as it is, by design). Env SBLAYOUT_OFF turns this off.

level_format._doc: A WORD LIST'S KIND IS READ PER LEVEL. Word defines a list's marker per level (w:lvl ilvl → numFmt): a numbered list often carries bulleted sub-points, and a bulleted list numbered ones. The kind was read from level 0 only, so a bulleted sub-level under a numbered list rendered as an <ol> («  1. Both sides look the same, like a mirror image.»). Each list paragraph now takes the kind of its own level (bullet → • / <ul>, any numbering format → 1. / <ol>); a level that defines none (numFmt none, or absent) keeps the level-0 kind. The table-cell numbered record (cellNumbered) reads it the same way. Env LISTLEVELFMT_OFF = level 0 for every level.

word_count._doc_reset: A HEADING ENDS A LIST'S CONTINUATION: a non-list paragraph opening with one of reset_tags (the writer's bracket tag, its first words) or carrying a Word heading style (reset_style_pattern) starts a new section, so every list counter starts again after it. Writers reuse one Word list for every activity's «Today we will:» steps (CEDT104), which Word numbers on; the human build restarts each one, as a list split only by a sentence, an image or a note keeps its numbers.
word_count._doc: WORD'S OWN LIST NUMBER. A paragraph in a Word numbered list is written with the number Word shows on it ("3. Why do these crusaders…"), not a blanket "1.": the extractor reads numbering.xml's counting facts (numId → abstract list, each level's w:start, each numId's w:startOverride) and advances one counter per abstract list and level in document order — a deeper level resets under a shallower item, an override restarts its level the first time its numId is met, empty and red numbered paragraphs count as Word counts them, and table-cell paragraphs are not counted. With the list renderer's ol_start, a list the writer interrupted (a sentence, an image, a writer note) continues at its own number — KB constraint 42: numbered steps use <ol><li> with start="N" for continuation across split content.

wrap_per_line._doc:
A STYLED RUN ACROSS THE WRITER'S SOFT LINE BREAK IS STYLED ON EACH LINE. A bold or italic run that holds a Word soft line break (w:br, a real newline in the run text) was wrapped once across the break ('**Strong g\nSoft g**'), and the per-line split downstream left '

**Strong g

Soft g**

': the markers shown to the learner and the style lost. Each line of such a run is wrapped on its own ('**Strong g**\n**Soft g**'), with the same leading / trailing space rule per line — here in the extractor, the one place that knows a real bold run from asterisks the writer typed (footnote marks «*», «**», «***»). bold / italic turn each half on. An answer mark that spans the break is matched with the markers allowed at each break (Utils.MarkAnswers). Env STYLEPERLINE_OFF = the single wrap.

run_toggle_forms._doc: A RUN'S BOLD / ITALIC IN EITHER XML FORM. Desktop Word writes <w:b/>; another serialiser writes the same element with a space before the closing slash (<w:b />, <w:b w:val="1" />) and may spell the on-value "on". With this block enabled the extractor's bold / italic test accepts optional whitespace before the slash and every value listed in on_values; disabled, or under the env toggle, it accepts the compact form with 1 / true only — and a document saved in the spaced form ships without any of the writer's bold or italic. w:val="0" / "false" stays off in both.

vert_align._doc: THE WRITER'S SUPERSCRIPT AND SUBSCRIPT. A Word run's <w:vertAlign w:val="superscript|subscript"/> is read, so CO₂ does not render as CO2 nor m² as m2. The gold carries the writer's non-ordinal superscripts (2, 1, -1, 3, +, - …) and subscripts (CBI's formulas), and writes ORDINAL suffixes plain. ON: DocxExtractor records the run's vertAlign; the black-run serialiser wraps a superscript / subscript piece in private-use sentinels (superscript U+E020…U+E021, subscript U+E022…U+E023) inside its bold / italic group — an ordinal suffix (ordinal_pattern after a digit) stays plain; PageAssembler turns them into <sup> / <sub> LAST (DocxExtractor.VertReplace, beside the equation MathReplace), keeps the plain text inside attribute values and <title>, and strips them from the .txt hand-off. Env VERTALIGN_OFF (the pieces carry no key — output unchanged).

whole_phrase._doc: 'Show them, with a guard for whole phrases'. Neighbouring raised (lowered) runs form ONE piece (joined across plain whitespace or a line break). A piece holding words — word_pattern (a 3+-letter word followed by more text) on its text, or two or more typed spaces — was raised by accident (as in ART1002's sentences, MXDI301's '(This is read as ten raised to the second power)', MXFUN02's '3rd  Smokey'): only its leading number / sign / short symbol (lead_pattern) is raised and the rest stays at normal height — as MXDI301's human build shows 10<sup>2</sup> (This is read …); with no such lead the piece stays plain. DocxExtractor.VertReplace.

needs_base._doc:
The base guard for whole phrases. A raised or lowered piece needs a BASE immediately before it (base_pattern on the text before it, past inline tags only): x², CO₂, 10⁻¹, Na⁺. One that opens a line, a table cell or a list item, or follows a space, is not an exponent or an index — ART1002's raised list words (
  • Maps
    • ; its gold writes them all flat) and MXDI301's cell line «10 raised to the 0 power» after a line break (gold 100
    10 raised to the 0 power) — and stays at normal height. Only read when whole_phrase is enabled.

after_index._doc: A RAISED PIECE RIGHT AFTER A LOWERED ONE HAS ITS BASE. An ion's charge is typed raised straight after the lowered count of its last atom — CO₃²⁻, SO₄²⁻, PO₄³⁻ (CBI1009's equations) — so the text right before the raised piece ends with the closing of the lowered piece, not a letter or digit, and the base guard dropped the charge to the line («CO<sub>3</sub>2-»). A raised piece whose text before it ends with a closed lowered piece (or a closed raised piece) has its base. Env SUPAFTERSUB_OFF.

underline._doc: THE WRITER'S UNDERLINE (KB 01C: `__text__` → `<u>text</u>`; 02C: underline markers converted to HTML tags). A black run's direct <w:u w:val="…"/> (any value but none) is read and ships as <u> — with the guard: only a piece INSIDE a sentence (its paragraph has other, non-underlined black text with a letter or digit); a whole underlined paragraph stays plain, and any heading stays plain (the sentinels are dropped inside <h1>–<h6>, attribute values and <title>). A hyperlink's own underline is never a <u> (a run inside a <w:hyperlink> or carrying a character style on link_styles is skipped); red writer text is untouched. The piece rides the black text as the U+E024 … U+E025 sentinel pair (whitespace kept outside; neighbouring pieces joined across plain whitespace) and becomes <u> last, in PageAssembler beside the superscript pass; the hand-off file gets plain text. A piece with no letter or digit (an underlined blank line of spaces) stays plain. Env UNDERLINE_OFF.
underline._doc_word_edges: An underlined PHRASE (its text holds a space) that starts or ends inside a word is the writer's selection slip («the d__ecimal number system__», «T__he base-10 …__») and takes the rest of that word; an underline inside one word (phonics letters «du__ck__s», a digit of a number) has no space and stays exactly as typed.
underline._doc_authoring_marks: Two underlines are the writer's authoring marks, not emphasis, and stay plain: a phrase whose next non-blank piece is a red writer instruction (before_instruction — `__techniques__ [definition: …]`, `__open question__ [roll-over definition: …]`: the underline shows which words the hover or link acts on, and the hover builder needs those words untouched), and any underline in a paragraph whose black text carries a raw address (url_pattern — `[Recording link] https://… __Please clip at:__`, a typed link label).

formatting_markers.note: Matches the parsed corpus conventions: **bold**, *italic*, '• ' bullets. Numbered list items keep their literal numbers.
formatting_markers.preserve_leading_space_note: (As in OSBY201-01.) A docx splits a styled phrase into its own run, and Word often keeps the inter-word SPACE INSIDE that styled run as a LEADING space (run 'their' has no trailing space; the bold run is ' wellbeing or hauora'). Wrapping a bold/italic run with blackText.trim() drops BOTH sides, so restoring only the TRAILING space would lose the leading one and glue the words ('theirwellbeing…', 'house orwhare'); the human build keeps the space before . When true, DocxExtractor#parseParagraph restores the leading space SYMMETRICALLY, only when the run actually had one, so legitimately-glued cases (no leading space) are untouched. Env BOLDSPACE_OFF uses the drop form.

body_strip._doc: THE TEMPLATE'S FRONT-MATTER FIELDS ARE NEVER LEARNER TEXT. When the writer's front-matter block sits after the content start (after an [End page] or inside the overview), its 'Label: value' lines shipped as body paragraphs — 'Curriculum Level: Phases 1, 2, 3, 4 (Y1-10)', 'Module code: TEFUN02', 'Key contacts: <a staff member's name and email>', 'Date submitted: 2024' (TEFUN02, TEFUN05; CEDR302 'Key contact: (Name), (email), (extension)', CHI1004); the human build shows none of them. PageAssembler (an item pre-pass): a free black paragraph whose text opens with one of these field labels is dropped.

front_matter_metadata.rule: The Section-A/B gray info table holds module-specific fields as 'Label: value' paragraphs in the front-matter (before content start). DocxExtractor captures the FILLED ones (a non-empty value after the colon) into run.metadata. This is the ONE place writers add module-specific data inside the otherwise-generic front-matter, so it is mined even though the front-matter is discarded for conversion.
front_matter_metadata.course_is_english_title_backup: The 'Course' value is the module's English course/title (e.g. 'AI Digital Citizenship'). Used as the English title BACKUP when the [TITLE BAR] payload contains only a Te Reo title — the module must NEVER ship with a Te-Reo-only title (as in OSAI301's [TITLE BAR] held only 'Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI').
front_matter_metadata.skip_empty_label_rows: A paragraph that is just 'Label:' with no value is the blank template row — never captured.

title_in_code_cell._note_mtk_title: The TRR1xx MTK front-matter table has no Module Name row; the Module Code cell reads 'TRR108: Ngā Orokati Tuarua – Final Consonants'. The text after the code token (and an optional colon/dash) is kept as metadata.moduleCodeTitle for PageAssembler's MTK title fallback (header.mtk_titles). The moduleCode field itself is unchanged. Env MTKTITLES_OFF.

front_matter_metadata._table_row_fields_note: The PNR family's front matter carries its metadata as a TABLE ('Module Name | Nga tau: 1 | Numbers: 1'), not 'Label: value' paragraphs. Only the fields listed here are captured from 2-column table rows (label cell | value cell) — deliberately NOT course/moduleCode, so the Course-is-title-backup path fires only on paragraph front matter. Used as the bilingual title source when the module has no [TITLE BAR] payload (PageAssembler; the value pipe-splits reo|english in payload order). Env REODROPMENU_OFF disables the table capture.

no_break_hyphen._doc: THE WRITER'S NON-BREAKING HYPHEN IS KEPT. Word stores a non-breaking hyphen (Ctrl+Shift+-) as its own element, <w:noBreakHyphen/>, not as text, so reading only the w:t text glued the words ('second‑hand' → 'secondhand', 'follow‑up' → 'followup'). The element is read as `char` at its own position (the human build writes a plain hyphen, 'ding-ding'). Env NBHYPHEN_OFF = the element is skipped.

tab_in_place._doc: THE WRITER'S TAB SEPARATES THE WORDS WHERE IT WAS TYPED. Word stores a tab as its own element, <w:tab/>, between the run's w:t texts ('1.' <w:tab/> 'Who lives closest …', 'big' <w:tab/><w:tab/> 'enormous'). Reading the run's text first and then putting ONE space before the whole run moved the tab to the run's start, so the words either side of it ran together ('1.Who lives closest …', 'bigenormous', '5VValue'). Each tab is read as a space at its own position in the run; a run of tabs is one space, and a run whose tabs all come before its text reads exactly as before (one leading space). Env TABINPLACE_OFF = the one leading space per run.

paragraph.rule:
A writer's Shift+Enter stores a INSIDE the paragraph; extracting only the w:t text would delete it, gluing the text on either side with no separator at all ('…ana”Through perseverance…') — corrupted text, and soft breaks are common in Writers Templates. When true, DocxExtractor contributes '\n' at the break's own position in the run text (a with type=page|column stays a page/column break — the page counter is untouched). The downstream machinery handles multi-line text: renderBlackText emits one

/

  • per line — the MAJORITY gold form for soft-broken black paragraphs (EXPFUN03 keeps its own house style); Utils.Fold collapses \s+ so tag classification is unaffected; the proverbSplit boundary rules stay dormant (the lines arrive already split). Env SOFTBR_OFF gives the glued extraction.

self_closed_skip.rule: Word writes an EMPTY paragraph as a SELF-CLOSED <w:p w14:paraId=".."/> (often in empty table cells inside a textbox, as in CHFUN01's Section A). If DocxExtractor.#findClose counted each as an OPEN with no matching close, the depth would ratchet up and a textbox-carrying paragraph's scan would run to end-of-body — the WHOLE module would collapse into ONE giant block: the front matter leaking into the output, every paragraph boundary lost (bullets glued, [tags] fused into prose), and IsContentStart never seeing the real [TITLE BAR]. When true, a self-closed <w:p .../> contributes NOTHING to the depth scan and is skipped as a top-level block (it has no content). A module with no self-closed paragraphs is unaffected BY CONSTRUCTION. Env toggle: SELFCLOSEP_OFF counts them as opens.

textbox_lift.rule: Word stores a text box (or any shape that holds text) TWICE inside <mc:AlternateContent> in a run of the paragraph that anchors it: the DrawingML copy in <mc:Choice> and a VML copy in <mc:Fallback> for older readers. Read in place, the anchoring paragraph closes at the box's first inner paragraph, so that inner paragraph is read as part of the anchor's run and takes the anchor run's colour (a box's black or white letter shown as a red note), the anchor's own words after the box are lost, and each box paragraph after the first is read twice, once per copy (a built widget showing every word twice). With this block enabled, before the walk, every <mc:AlternateContent> that holds a <w:txbxContent> is taken out of its run and the content of each text box in ONE copy (copy: the <mc:Choice> copy, or the <mc:Fallback> copy when the Choice holds no text box) is placed right after the close of the anchoring paragraph, in document order, so every box paragraph is read once, on its own; a text box inside a text box is lifted the same way (up to max_passes). inline_in_place: an INLINE box (<wp:inline> — it sits in the line like a character) of one paragraph with the anchor's words on both sides keeps its runs in place, so the sentence reads through it ('Select [Run >].'). scope body: a text box inside a table cell is left where it is (a table cell joins its paragraphs with its own separator and prints red spans as cell text, so a box lifted inside a cell would show new separators and the writer's instructions). No embedded image is read from either copy. Disabled, or under the env toggle, the copies are walked in place.

math.rule: KB 05A 'MathJax / Equations': an equation is emitted as MathML — the gold's form and the one that renders in MTK. A Word equation is not a w:r run — it lives in an <m:oMath> beside the runs of a w:p (in the Writers Templates every equation is inline beside runs; none uses <m:oMathPara>), so a run walk alone never sees it and the equation would vanish from the page. Each <m:oMath> is converted by OmmlMathml (the pageforge-site/js/omml-to-mathml.js port; vocabulary r/t, f, sSup, sSub, d, rad covers the OMML the templates use, the rest of the grammar is implemented anyway and an unknown element is recursed as <mrow>, never dropped) and replaced IN PLACE by a synthetic black run carrying a private-use sentinel (U+E010 <id> U+E011) that flows through every text path — tag classification, coalescing, the emoji strip, the hover sentinels U+E000/E001, the typed-number list — unchanged; PageAssembler's final post-pass swaps the sentinel for the <math xmlns=…> markup (bare — the gold's majority form, inline far more often than block; MathJax renders it either way) and adds body_class_token to the <body> class of every page that carries a <math> (the gold's per-page form); the hand-off .txt gets the same swap. Every page with a <math> carries mathJax, and no sentinel reaches the page. Env MATHML_OFF turns it off (the equations are then dropped).

typed_fractions._doc_slash_pattern: No whitespace around the slash: a table cell's lines reach the page joined by ' / ' (MXEO301's order-of-operations cells `– 32 / 3² = …`), so a spaced slash is a line separator, never a fraction. A number may carry thousands separators (`1/1,000` is one fraction, never `1/1` + `,000`).
typed_fractions._doc_vulgar: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a fraction CHARACTER the writer typed (½ ¼ ¾ …) is mostly kept as the character by the level-3 gold (MXDB302, MXFL301, MXFU301, MXEO301 …; MXFL302 alone converts its fractions) — it already renders as a fraction. A map entry here (`"½": [1, 2]`) would convert that character too; the code supports it, the data leaves it off.
typed_fractions.rule: KB CL-0115 (05A 'Equations'): THE WRITER'S TYPED FRACTION IN A LEVEL 3–4 MATHS MODULE IS EMITTED AS MathML. The gold carries <math> in modules whose Writers Templates hold no Word equation (MXFL302, MXFU301, MXFU402, MXDB302 …); most of them are fractions the writer TYPED as text (`1/1 = 1.0 = 100%`, `½ = 0.5`). In the Maths WTs the gold uses MathML for almost every typed fraction at level 3 (template 7-8) and level 4 (9-10), but plain text at level 2 and mostly in MXFUN (so those groups keep the plain text). The KB's output is always MathML with `mathJax` on the <body>; its example writes a single number as a bare <mn> (also the gold's majority form). A PER-GROUP rule keyed on run.groupKey (subject | template, ModuleResolver): in a TEXT segment of the page (the pre-acks slice), a typed `a/b` (1–4 digits each; never inside a date, path, URL, word, money or decimal — `slash_pattern`) or a vulgar fraction (`vulgar`) becomes <math xmlns=…><mfrac><mn>a</mn><mn>b</mn></mfrac></math>, the rest of the text untouched (the writer's words are kept; only the fraction's typography changes). Never inside `skip_zones` (scripts / styles / title, an existing <math>, a select / textarea / button / link, the developer notes) or an element carrying a `skip_class_tokens` class (the hand-off boxes — the developer's raw text). A page that gains a <math> gains `math.body_class_token` (the same condition as a Word equation). ListsAndRuns.TypedFractions, called by PageAssembler just before DocxExtractor.MathReplace. Env TYPEDFRAC_OFF turns it off.

text_normalise.rule: Word documents carry invisible whitespace characters the writer never intended as content: the NON-BREAKING SPACE U+00A0 (autocorrect/paste residue — the developer flagged it as an 'AI marker', as in SCCH302's [TITLE BAR] Te Reo) and the ZERO-WIDTH characters U+200B/U+200C/U+200D/U+FEFF (paste residue from web sources). NBSPs appear in almost every Writers Template, while the gold library carries effectively no literal NBSPs (the human's ' ' ENTITIES are deliberate layout, not writer residue). When enabled, DocxExtractor normalises each run's decoded w:t text at extraction (the same seam as the soft-break handling): U+00A0 → a plain space (nbsp_to_space), and the zero-width set is deleted (strip_zero_width). GRANULARITY SAFETY: an NBSP-only run stays a non-empty whitespace piece (same trim()/Fold behaviour either way — JS whitespace includes U+00A0), so red-span merging is untouched; a run the zero-width strip EMPTIES drops out exactly like an always-empty run, so tag spans are unchanged. Tag CLASSIFICATION is unaffected by construction either way (Utils.Fold collapses \s+, and \s matches U+00A0). Env NBSP_OFF turns off the whole normalisation (NBSPs and zero-width characters flow through to the page).

answer_marks._doc_occurrence_index: The answer-key carry-through: each mark also records nth — how many times its text already occurred in the paragraph's plain text before it (in a table cell, the cell's earlier paragraphs counted too) — so Utils.MarkAnswers can place it when the same words occur twice on a line (ARFUN04 3N: the label '**Contrast:**' and the answer '(Contrast/Emphasis)'). Side-channel only; env ANSWERKEY_OFF.
answer_marks.rule: Besides RED text, writers mark the correct answer of a quiz with a yellow HIGHLIGHTER (<w:highlight>) or with GREEN text (00b050 — distinct from the template's own guidance green 316757, which stays ignored; OSAH401 uses 00b050 for exactly its announced answers). This channel records those marks as a SEPARATE side-channel — block.marks = [{text, kind: 'hl'|'green'}] on a paragraph block (consecutive same-kind marked runs merge, a pure-whitespace gap bridges), and block.cellMarks (rows-aligned per cell) on a table block — WITHOUT touching block.text by a single byte, so tag granularity, red-span structure and every existing consumer are unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION. 'white' highlight is template guidance chrome (the OS-family 'Refer to How to Merge Content.pdf' lines) and never a mark. NO consumer acts on a mark without its own fence: the dropDown reading requires the writer's own ANNOUNCEMENT ('Correct answers highlighted' / 'Correct answers in green') in the same bundle — essential, because highlight is also used editorially (TRR109's whole-paragraph highlights) and green marks the OPTIONS themselves on OSAI101, where reading it as an answer would build a WRONG quiz. Env ANSMARK_OFF turns the channel off (no marks recorded, every consumer dormant).

render_text.rule:
TagNormaliser.RenderText extracts the ORIGINAL-CASE text a writer left OUTSIDE the brackets of a tag span (e.g. '[H1] INTRODUCTION' -> 'INTRODUCTION'). When the writer glues a STRAY PUNCTUATION character to the tag and nothing else ('[whakatauki]:' -> ':', as in OSAH501-00), that residue is NOT content — it is writer noise — and would otherwise leak downstream as an embedded LEAD (a spurious '

:

' before the proverb in the whakataukī box). When true, a RenderText result that contains NO letter or digit in ANY script (Unicode \p{L}/\p{N} — macrons ā/ē/ī/ō/ū count as letters, so te reo is never dropped) is treated as EMPTY (''), so the noise vanishes and any '|| blackAfter' fallback chain falls through to the real content. ROBUST + GENERAL: handles any erroneous glued character (':', ';', '-', '.', '|', '(', ']', '*', '…') across EVERY tag and EVERY RenderText caller, not just whakataukī. CONSERVATIVE: a residue with even one letter/digit (a real embedded title/label) is untouched. The human never renders a punctuation-only lead. Env STRAYLEAD_OFF lets the punctuation residue through.

emoji_strip.disclosure: Emoji have been removed from this content per the no-emoji rule. Ticks and crosses are retained.
emoji_strip.rule:
Change Ledger CL-0051 (the first CL-0001/constraint-1 exception permitting deletion of writer characters). Emoji are stripped from rendered writer content: ListsAndRuns.EmojiStrip runs as a FULL-PAGE POST-PASS (after OmitPlaceholderResidue + TidyDeveloperNotes, before LinkTextDisplay/Indent, stopping at the acks block), so every emitter is covered uniformly and NO pre-render machinery can be disturbed: tag classification, the ✅-glued [TITLE BAR] fences (OSSC301), the ✅[Tile] delimiters, the title splits and the 🔴 red-run sentinels all operate on block text long before this pass — post-pass placement makes them untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION. SCOPE = Unicode Extended_Pictographic grapheme CLUSTERS (base + VS15/16, skin tones U+1F3FB-FF, ZWJ sequences, keycap marks; regional-indicator flag pairs; a keycap digit keeps its digit and loses only the dressing), matched cluster-whole so a VS16 is NEVER orphan-stripped off a kept tick. 'exempt' = the ledger's ticks & crosses VERBATIM (✓✗✘ are not Extended_Pictographic and could never match anyway — listed for fidelity). 'exempt_extensions.maths_operators' = the ONE extension (✖➗➕➖ — meaning-bearing operators in maths content; the gold keeps ✖; ✖ is a cross by form, and the ledger's own ☑ inclusion shows heavy/box variants count). 'arrow_map' = EP arrow emoji become PLAIN arrows instead of deletions (gold's own treatment — TEDC402 ships the writer's 'input🡪process🡪output' as 'input→process→output'; meaning kept, emoji removed). OUT OF SCOPE by the Unicode property: the checkbox/ballot family ☐☒□🗹 (bilingual checklists + printable tick-sheets; the checklist→bullet conversion stays with the reo-menu machinery), 🖵 phonics sound-boxes (BLL147), 🡪 (TEDC401 gold keeps it), plain →←, typographic ►●◦, private-use chars — none are emoji per Extended_Pictographic. CLAUSES: a run of 2+ consecutive PLAIN

lines each PREFIXED by a would-be-deleted cluster becomes ONE

    of
  • (the lead cluster dropped; as in CEDT104 '🎵Sing/🎵Do/🎵Feel', ARFUN02's instrument list; an exempt-led line like '✅ I did it.' never joins a run and stays a

    ); a LONE prefixed line stays a

    ; in-prose clusters are removed with spacing normalised (doubled spaces collapsed, space-before-punctuation healed — 'earn a star ⭐️.' → 'earn a star.'); a plain

    the strip EMPTIED is dropped whole (drop_emptied — as in ARFUN02's

    🤔

    , which the gold never keeps; a PRE-EXISTING empty

    is never touched). DISCLOSURE: ONE visible note per affected page at the first removal, ledger wording verbatim in 'disclosure', emitted through NotesAndComments.redFlag (kind diagnostic → 'Red Flag:' prefix, red+bold, class cv2-note; NOTESCHEME_OFF legacy form applies to it like any note); a first removal inside the header/menu relocates the note to the top of the body (the no-comments-in-menu rule). CONTAINMENTS: cv2-interactive placeholder subtrees (the developer's verbatim hand-off), cv2-note/cv2-comment payloads (writer quotes stay verbatim), the acks block (gold keeps oEmbed video titles verbatim + the converter's own ❗ ack-todo markers are functional chrome),

module_code_detection._doc: ModuleResolver.DetectModuleCode reads the module code with one regex — 2-6 letters + 2-4 digits (+RR) — over the filenames, then the first front-matter paragraphs. Some codes fall outside it: CHWHA / GEWHA (no digits), ANZHFUN05 (seven letters), PWYWHA1 (one digit — and its front matter mentions PWY1000, so it would convert AS PWY1000). Such builds would be named MODULE_0_0.html / PWY1000_0_0.html and their registry rows never reached (global defaults instead). registry_token: between the filename regex and the front-matter regex, each filename's LEADING token (split on `separators`, upper-cased) that is a key of Module_Structure_Index.module_meta is a candidate — a code the regex cannot shape still resolves when the corpus registry knows it. The regex keeps precedence (an unchanged path for every module it already names); the front-matter regex stays the last resort. Env CODEREG_OFF uses the regex-only detection.

wt_page_tracking.rule: Each content block is stamped with the Writers Template page it sits on, counted from: w:lastRenderedPageBreak elements (Word's own pagination record), explicit w:br type='page', and w:pageBreakBefore paragraph properties that are TRUE (bare element or val='1'/'true' — Google-Docs exports write val='0' meaning NO break; never count those).
wt_page_tracking.reliability_note: Google-Docs-exported templates (verified on OSAH401) carry NO usable pagination records, so page numbers may stay at 1. The acks lesson-mapping therefore treats page records as only ONE evidence source — see media_item_lesson_mapping below.
wt_page_tracking.page_records_usable_when: the counted page total is at least min_pages_for_trust

media_item_lesson_mapping.rule: Mapping a media item to its lesson (for acksLesson grouping) uses the strongest available evidence, in order. Guessing is banned; every interpolated or fallback placement is reported in the conversion summary.
order: 1. CONTENT MATCH — the item's normalised URL (or unique asset ID) appears in exactly one lesson's content blocks → that lesson.
2. PAGE RECORDS — when the WT docx has usable pagination (see wt_page_tracking), the item's WTPg No. falls in one lesson's page span → that lesson.

3. NEIGHBOUR INTERPOLATION — media lists run in page order; an unmatched item between two items mapped to the SAME lesson belongs to that lesson. Between different lessons → the earlier lesson, and the placement is reported in the summary.
4. FALLBACK — remaining items go to the first content group, each reported in the summary (never dropped).

unsupported_pathways.where: any paragraph before content start, folded
unsupported_pathways.label: MTK / Te Reo Rangatira (TRR) bilingual template
unsupported_pathways.action: Do not convert. Surface a clear visible notice in the conversion summary: this template follows a separate bilingual pathway (paired reo/eng elements) and must not be force-fitted through the standard rules.
unsupported_pathways.note: The 'MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE' heading ALSO appears in standard templates' front-matter (verified on OSAH401), so the signature alone is not enough — the module code prefix must match too.

media_table.identify_rule: A docx table is THE media table when its first row matches at least min_header_matches of the column families below (folded, punctuation-insensitive). In a combined WT+media-list docx the media table is located anywhere in the document and is excluded from content conversion.

strip_markers._note: The media-table cell cleaner also strips the extractor's **bold** / *italic* asterisk markers before the header fold and the row parse (never an underscore — a URL character, as in Pita_Sharples in a Wikimedia link). Some modules (BLL120–BLL123) type the header cells bold; without the strip the exact alias match would never fire and the module would parse NO media list at all (its [Item N] references, iStock filenames and acks entries unresolved; the table rendered as a kept <table> on the last lesson page). A marker the extractor added is never a header word or a URL character; the gold's acks never carry one. Env MLMARKERS_OFF leaves the markers in.

example_row.rule: Drop any data row matching the template's worked example: item_no folded equals 'example', OR the description contains an example_signature.

discard_rows.reminder_rows: Drop any full-width/merged row (a row with a single spanning cell) and any row whose first cell starts with 'reminder' — these are writer guidance, not items.
discard_rows.header_row: The first (header) row itself is never an item.
discard_rows.empty_rows: Drop rows where every cell is blank.

media_table.hyperlinks: URLs are usually Word hyperlinks: the visible cell text may be truncated or decorative — ALWAYS resolve the run's w:hyperlink r:id against word/_rels/document.xml.rels (TargetMode='External') and prefer the rel Target over visible text.
media_table.description_caution: The Description column is the writer's own wording — NEVER use it as an acknowledgement {Title} for stock assets (Acks_Formats.json title_authority).

input_shapes.separate: Two files: one docx containing a [TITLE BAR] (the WT), one docx whose only substance is the media table (the media list).
input_shapes.combined: One docx containing both the [TITLE BAR] content and a media table.
input_shapes.classification_rule: Per uploaded file: has content_start fragment → WT; has media table but no content start → media list; has both → combined. Neither → red flag in summary (unrecognised document). A docx with no content start whose table opens with the two-cell header 'Section heading | Text/Activity' is the ACTIVITY-TABLE dialect (activity_table below) — a Writers Template in a different dialect, recognised as the WT and refused BY NAME (it has no adapter yet) instead of falling into 'unrecognised'.
input_shapes.no_media_list: If no media table is found anywhere, still generate the acknowledgements block (standing items + per-lesson designer-media check lines) and surface a clear summary warning.

activity_table.label: Activity-table Writers Template (the XOTP reader family — a 'Section heading | Text/Activity' table, no red tags)
activity_table.action: Recognised as a Writers Template in the ACTIVITY-TABLE dialect: the left cell of each row (Overview / Introduction / Online book / Questions / a bare activity number …) carries the structure that red tags carry in the standard template. The adapter that turns that table into PageForge's tag stream is not enabled yet (input_shapes.activity_table.adapter) — nothing converted; see 00-NEW_NEW_NEW/_SPEC__XOTP_Activity_Table_Template.md.

adapter._note: The adapter (text only). DocxExtractor.AdaptActivityTable turns the activity table into the synthetic red-tag paragraph stream the whole existing pipeline already speaks (TITLE BAR / LESSON N / Lesson Overview / H2 / H3 / Body / alert / Activity / the widget invocations / button / End page), so no builder, no menu shell and no page-splitter rule is new. The mapping is DATA: the section lexicon below (left-cell text → role), the widget hints (row text → invocation tag), the page-break rule and the instruction handling. The reader book (carousel images, the picture / sentence matching payload, the acks credits) is NOT in any of the XOTP documents — those widgets render as the standard hand-off placeholders (a Media List for the family would be needed).
adapter._sections_note: Tested in order against the FOLDED left cell (bold / underline markers and parenthetical notes removed, lines joined by ' / '); the first match wins; a row matching nothing is emitted as an [Activity] too (a section heading with no number — the G writers' 'Word Challenge' / 'Sequence Activity' rows carry their number on a second line, caught by the trailing-number pattern). The Quiz row and its nested 'I can' table are the D2L self-assessment quiz — never a page (spec §3.2); recorded in the run notes. The Quiz row is TERMINAL: the extractor flattens the nested 'I can' table's six rows into the outer table after it, so nothing after the Quiz row is read.
adapter._page_title_note: Every gold XOTP page's own h1 repeats the module title (XOTPG04_1_0 / _2_0: two identical `My Drum Kit` spans), so the adapted pages skip the PageSplitter heading harvest (which would take the Introduction [H2]) and the SkeletonBuilder module-title fallback applies.
adapter._no_overview_page_note: The gold's first file is 1_0 — there is no overview page; the writer's Overview row is the lesson-page module menu. The splitter's RR-4 normally merges a title-bar-only opening segment forward AS the overview (label 0.0); with this flag the segment folds into lesson 1 as a LESSON page (PageSplitter, run.noOverviewPage), so the files pair with the gold's 1_0 / 2_0 and the title still resolves from the title-bar item riding on page 1.
adapter._widget_hints_note: Matched in order over the folded text of the WHOLE row (left + right cells) — the section heading decides the widget, a CS: line only confirms it (spec §3.4: the six G / O modules carry no CS: line at all). No hint → a plain [Activity] box (Kei a koe, the Syllable Count / Word Challenge charts, whose gold is a table the writer only linked).

overview_list_after_label._note:
The Overview cell's success-criteria items are typed as PLAIN paragraphs (no numPr, no style — as in the docx of XOTPG04 / G01 / O01), so they would reach the two-column item menu as

lines; the gold renders them as

  • on every page that has them and the KB fixes the form — 01B_MODULE_MENUS_FOOTER (`
    I can:
    ` + `
    • `), constraint 23. The lines after a label matching label_match (folded) up to the next bold label or the first line of >= stop_min_words words take the corpus bullet prefix, so ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText groups them into ONE

overview_link_only_todo.note: Designer/Developer To Do: paste the overview from the linked Google Doc ({url}) — the Writers Template gives only its link.
overview_link_only_todo._doc: A To Do placeholder rather than pasting the text. XOTPB08–13's Overview cell holds 'In this module, ākonga will:' and then ONLY a link — 'Overview Set 2-Emergent' → a Google Doc — so the menu would show the bare link label as a paragraph. An Overview line whose text is exactly a row link's label, where that link points at a Google Doc (url_match), becomes a red line carrying this note; red_flag.todo_lead renders it under the ledger's 'Designer/Developer To Do:' prefix. The XOTPG wording is NOT reused (its 'I can' goals differ). Env XOTPOVERVIEW_OFF keeps the bare label.

adapter._family_note: The XOTP family's page conventions, as the gold pages show them: the Story-Questions alert's title is the callout's own lead (`callouts.by_tag.alert.variants` fixes it at h3 with no inner row and a col-md-9 column) and its questions are the writer's DECIMAL list (the docx numId → decimal; a table cell carries no numFmt, so the extractor marks every cell list `• ` — `questions_list: numbered` restores `1. ` and renderBlackText builds the <ol>); every activity box holds its content DIRECTLY (`activity_box: bare` → run.activityBoxBare → activity_wrapper.open_bare); the lesson h1 repeats the module title (the pages carry two identical `<h1><span>` — `lesson_title_repeats_module` → run.lessonTitleRepeatsModule, honoured where the registry h1_count asks for 2); a writer [H2] keeps its digit (keep_writer_digit.digits_by_prefix.2 += XOTP). Not taken: the gold's body `<h2><span>` wrapper (the corpus no_span_rule), the acks on the LAST page (the KB puts it on the overview — the first page here), the I-can items as a <ul> (plain paragraphs in the docx, the human's editorial bullets).
adapter._button_note: The Share row's 'Upload to dropbox button         Go to assessment quiz button' line: every label ends in the word 'button', so the line splits on that word and each part becomes one [button] (the dropbox post-pass then adds the box's class token from the 'dropbox' label).
adapter._page_break_note: Spec §3.3: no [End page] anywhere, yet every module ships exactly two pages. Lettered labels (the G / O variant: 1A 1B 1C 2A 2B 2C) break where the lesson digit changes — derivable from the labels themselves; bare numbers (the B variant: 1 2 3 4 5) break after row 3 (verified on all six B modules). The overview row's content is repeated as each lesson page's [Lesson Overview] block — the writer's '(dropdown at top right)' is the lesson-page module menu, and the gold has no overview page.
adapter._cs_line_note: A row line opening `CS:` / `To CS:` is the writer's note to Creative Services (`CS: Create a drag and drop activity:`) — emitted as a RED span so the standard instruction path renders the Writers Note; it never becomes body prose.
adapter._parenthetical_note: A line that is wholly parenthetical — '(Answers in order: Look, seeds, …)', '(Please position the think bubble above the photo at left)' — is the writer's instruction to the developer, never page text: it is emitted as a red bracket-less span, which the normaliser classifies as an instruction and the note scheme surfaces as a Writers Note. A 'CS:' / 'To CS:' line stays a plain paragraph: the addressee-prefix scheme already renders it as a Writers Note (the spec's two editorial CS: lines therefore survive as notes, exactly as the spec asks).

activity_table._note: XOTP recognition (spec _SPEC__XOTP_Activity_Table_Template.md §3.1 / §6). The XOTP documents (XOTPB08–13, XOTPG01, XOTPG03–06, XOTPO01) carry NO square-bracket red tags; the structure lives in one two-column table whose header row is 'Section heading | Text/Activity' (the table opens with a merged title row, so the header is the SECOND row — scan_rows). The header pair exists only in the XOTP Writers Templates, so the detector is exact and has no effect on any other module by construction. DocxExtractor.IsActivityTableDoc reads it; ModuleResolver.PrepareRun takes such a document as the WT when the standard chain found none, and — with adapter.enabled false — returns the data-driven 'unsupported' refusal (label / action above) that batch_convert reports as 'refused by design' and the App renders in the summary, in place of the misleading 'no Writers Template (no content opener found)'. Same header test as pageforge-site/js/formatter.js OutputFormatter.ACTIVITY_TABLE_NOTICE (the parsed-text tab). Env ACTTABLE_OFF uses the plain 'no-wt' path.

repeat_tables._doc: EVERY MEDIA TABLE THAT CARRIES THE TEMPLATE'S OWN MEDIA-LIST PREAMBLE LEAVES THE CONTENT STREAM: MXEX101 pastes the template's media-list section (the red 'MEDIA LIST' heading, 'Please supply details for ALL external media …', the copyright bullet, the media table) after several lessons, and the trim above removes only the one media table ModuleResolver identifies — the rest would open implicit pages holding the preamble as Writers Notes. After that trim, every further media table (MediaListParser.FindMediaTable) with a phrases_exact / phrases_contains hit within max_blocks before it is trimmed the same way (TrimMediaListPreamble), up to max_tables. A media table with no such preamble (ENGJ402 / MXEO202's journal media lists, HIS1006's resource-pack tables) stays. Seen in MXEX101, MXFUN01, MUS1004. Env MLREPEAT_OFF.

submission_checklist._doc: THE TEMPLATE'S SUBMISSION CHECKLIST NEVER SHIPS. The Writers Template ends with its own checklist for the writer ('SUBMISSION CHECKLIST' / 'Have you:' / '☐ Completed Section A …', '☐ Checked the resource code is correct?' …), which the human build never shows. The tail rule above drops it only when it is the first thing after the media table; a writer's note between the two (CEDT404's permission-form link, CEDO402's journal image links, CEDW201's permission forms), a checklist the extractor does not see as the tail (CBI1008, CHI1004's bulleted heading) or the old template's checklist followed by its writing guide (ANZH103) let it reach the last lesson page. A paragraph matching heading_pattern (red markers, bold / italic markers and edge whitespace removed) leaves the content with every following paragraph that is blank, equals a line_exact entry or contains a line_phrases entry, provided at least min_lines of them are checklist lines (a learner-facing assessment checklist under the same heading keeps its own lines and is left alone); the first other block stops the drop (the writer's notes before the heading and anything after the checklist are untouched). Env CHECKLIST_OFF.

phrases_contains: please supply details for all external media
media_list_preamble._forms_note: Three shapes: (1) the table in THIS document — the walk goes backwards from it; (2) no_table_heading — the WT carries the template's 'MEDIA LIST' heading + its instructions but the table is in a separate Media List docx (CHFUN01/04/05/06/07): the run is taken FORWARD from the heading and needs at least one contains-phrase after it; (3) label_max_words — a short plain label the writer puts on the table ('Phase 1', MXFUN03) is passed over between the preamble and the table (never above the preamble), and tail_extra_media_tables drops a SECOND media table that follows the first with only labels / blanks between (the same column test MediaListParser uses).
media_list_preamble._tail_note: The template's SUBMISSION CHECKLIST ('Have you: ☐ Completed Section A …') follows the media table on 81 of the 277 combined WTs and rendered as learner-facing text on 22 pages (gold 0). It is dropped with the table when the first non-blank block after the table opens with a tail_start_phrases entry AND every block to the end of the document is a paragraph carrying no red span that resolves to a tail_structural_directives tag other than [body] — the AR-5 substance test, so a media table placed mid-document (MXFUN01/02/03: Phase 2 content follows it) keeps its tail by construction. 175 combined WTs have nothing after the table; the ~20 with other trailing prose (an asset list, a stray URL) are left as they are.
media_list_preamble.rule: In a COMBINED Writers Template + Media List docx the media-list section opens after the last content page with a red 'MEDIA LIST' heading, the red 'Please supply details for ALL external media …' instruction and a plain-text copyright-clearance bullet ('If a specific third-party item/image is crucial to your writing, then please submit this for early copyright clearance …' with its sharepoint link), then the media TABLE. ModuleResolver.PrepareRun excludes only the table from the content stream, so without this the preamble would flow into the LAST LESSON PAGE: the two red runs would become Writers Notes and the bullet would render as learner-facing body text. The human gold never shows it, and almost every WT carries the bullet. DocxExtractor.TrimMediaListPreamble walks BACKWARDS from the media table: a paragraph block that is blank, whose folded text (red markers stripped) equals a phrases_exact entry, or contains a phrases_contains entry, is preamble; the walk stops at the first block matching none (a writer's [End] / [body] / prose) and at max_blocks. The preamble and the table are removed together; at least one phrase hit is required (blank lines alone never trigger it). A SEPARATE Media List docx is untouched by construction (its table is not among the WT's blocks). New preamble wording = a phrase added HERE. Env MLPREAMBLE_OFF drops the table block only.

trailing_content.rule: Content after the final [end page] containing no headings and no interactives is writer-form boilerplate (copyright checklist tables etc.) — emit nothing; record one summary note. Trailing empty tables are always discarded.
